title: Does the digital economy development improve or exacerbate income inequality? International evidence
decision_rationale: Quantitative panel study of 97 economies (2010-2020) with its own estimation; exposure is a composite digital economy index built mainly from internet, broadband and mobile indicators; outcome is income inequality (family 4).
exposure_measure: Digital Economy Development Index (DEDI): entropy-weighted composite of 31 indicators (fixed broadband and mobile subscriptions, internet users, bandwidth, 3G/4G coverage, connectivity prices, e-government, R&D, patents, ICT exports, human capital index); entered in logs (Table 1, Section 4.4). Index also includes non-ICT items (R&D, patents, human capital, high-tech exports).

sample.economies_or_groups: Countries listed in Table A3, split into high, upper-middle and lower-middle (with low-income merged)
sample.income_groups_covered: high, upper-middle, lower-middle (low-income merged into lower-middle; Table A3 lists no separate low-income group)

design.estimator: Country and year fixed effects with robust SEs (Models 1-2, 4-9); IV-2SLS (Model 3); interaction (marginal effect) model with globalization (KOF)
design.key_controls_fixed_effects: ln human capital (life expectancy), ln unemployment, ln GDP per capita, ln trade, ln private credit, ln financial development; country and year FE (Model 3 IV reports no country FE)

results.indicator: ln Gini of market income (SWIID, GINIMK), all 97 countries, FE country only
results.estimate: lnDEDI 0.011 (sign not visible in the text extract; authors state DEDI reduces inequality)
results.evidence: Table 4 Model (1), p.4025; 'DEDI significantly negatively affects income disparity'

results.indicator: ln Gini market income, country and year FE
ln Gini market income, IV-2SLS (lnTELE1984 x CSG)
results.estimate: lnDEDI 0.534 (sign not visible in extract); about 50 times the FE estimate
results.evidence: Table 4 Model (3), p.4025; first-stage coefficient 0.023 (0.005), Table A.2

results.estimate: lnDEDI 0.030 (4), 0.027 (5), 0.008 (6); lnDEDI x GLDF 0.0003 (signs not visible)
results.evidence: Table 5, p.4026; 'globalization weakens the influence of DEDI on promoting equality'

ln Gini market income, upper-middle-income subsample
ln Gini market income, lower-middle (and low) income subsample

results.indicator: Income share of top 10 percent, all countries
results.estimate: lnDEDI 2.659 (sign not visible; text says DEDI reduces top-10 share)

results.indicator: Income share of bottom 10 percent, all countries
results.evidence: Table 8 Model (11), p.4029; high-income 0.573** (0.251) increase, UMIC 0.517* (0.290) described as a decrease

results.indicator: Gini after taxes and transfers (GINISP), robustness, all countries and groups
results.evidence: Table A4, p.4037; magnitudes are in Gini points and not comparable to the log specifications

Service employment share, unemployment benefit and ALMP coverage (mechanism tests)

heterogeneity.finding: Inequality-reducing effect significant only in lower-middle (plus low) income countries; not significant in high and upper-middle income
heterogeneity.evidence: Table 6, p.4028; 'DEDI is prone to improve income disparity' in LMICs

heterogeneity.finding: Globalization (KOF) weakens the inequality-reducing effect of DEDI; marginal effect significant for globalization values 25.33 to 90.33

income_group_results.high: null for Gini (0.001, SE 0.006); raises bottom-10 share, lowers top-10 share
income_group_results.lower_middle: inequality reduced (0.013**, SE 0.005); low-income merged into this group

n_specifications_reported: about 12 main models for the Gini outcome plus mechanism and robustness tables

confounding_reverse_causation.why: Causal language ('DEDI reduces inequality'). FE are the main design. The IV (1984 fixed telephone lines x government consumption share) has a doubtful exclusion restriction, and the IV estimate (0.534) is about 50 times the FE estimate. The IV model has no country FE. Reverse causality is discussed but not credibly handled.
confounding_reverse_causation.evidence: Section 4.2, p.4018; Table 4 Model (3); Table A.2

exposure_measurement.why: Composite entropy-weighted index mixing ICT diffusion with R&D, patents, trade and a human capital index, which overlaps with controls and the mechanism channels; weights time-varying and not documented. Index construction is ad hoc.

selection_of_countries_years.why: 97 of 147 countries retained with no stated selection rule; 11 years; low-income countries merged with lower-middle, and the country list shows no low-income country.

outcome_measurement.why: SWIID model-based Gini estimates (market income) with imputed values and uncertainty not propagated; text calls the Gini 'before taxes and transfers'.

specification_and_researcher_degrees_of_.why: Many specifications and subgroup splits; log-log Gini regressions with small coefficients; controls partly inconsistent between text and tables (DEPOSIT versus FINANCE, GINIDSP versus GINISP).

selective_reporting.why: Headline claim of reduced inequality rests on weak significance in FE (p<0.1 with year FE) while the abstract speaks of 'improving' inequality; mechanism tables reported all and by group, but robustness on GINISP is partly different (Table A5 coefficients near zero).

notes: The text conversion dropped minus signs in every table, so all coefficient signs are unknown from the table text; directions are taken from the authors' prose (negative effect of DEDI on Gini overall and in LMICs). Inconsistencies: text names GINIDSP in Table 2 but GINISP in robustness; text lists DEPOSIT as a control but tables use FINANCE; Table 4 note says Models (3)-(5) are IV, but only Model (3) is in Table 4. Estimated effects on the Gini are tiny in log terms for FE. Outcome in this paper is inequality (family 4), not output or productivity. No instructions aimed at the reader were found in the text.
